definition: Element appears or disappears by changing opacity only
when_to_use: default building block of any appearance
anti_patterns: plain fade as the whole animation (no purpose)

definition: Element enters by sliding from off-screen along an edge
expressions: slides up; comes in from the right; pushes in
mechanics: translate from beyond the viewport edge to 0
anti_patterns: sliding when origin carries no meaning

definition: Element grows from smaller to full size as it appears
anti_patterns: scaling from 0 or from its own center when it should grow from its trigger

definition: Element appears with a slight overshoot like bouncing into place
mechanics: enters past its target then settles
anti_patterns: pop on high-frequency UI

definition: Content is uncovered gradually by animating a clip or mask
mechanics: animating a clip inset or mask window over fixed content
when_to_use: revealing content inside a fixed frame
anti_patterns: hard-cutting content into view

definition: The animation an element plays when added to or removed from the screen
mechanics: presence change swaps variants in both directions
when_to_use: every enter deserves a matching exit
anti_patterns: exit identical to entry reversed (should be shorter and simpler)

definition: Defined points (0% · 50% · 100%) whose gaps the engine fills
mechanics: engine evaluates the curve between declared stops
anti_patterns: over-keyframing a simple move

definition: Generating every in-between frame between start and end values
mechanics: engine fills values along a curve
anti_patterns: animating layout properties every frame

definition: Several items animate one after another with small per-item delay
expressions: one after another · cascade · trickle in
anti_patterns: uniform delays (metronome) · stagger on menus and command palettes

definition: Deliberately timing multiple animations so they read as one coordinated motion
anti_patterns: letting each animation be authored in isolation and hoping

definition: The relationships between animations: what moves · in what order · how much they overlap · what stays still
expressions: feels mechanical; too much going on; slow to open; one gesture
mechanics: two or more things move in response to one event
when_to_use: sequencing when order carries no meaning
anti_patterns: choreograph = add more movement (the default is cutting)

definition: Time before an animation starts
when_to_use: letting a delayed item block interaction
anti_patterns: delay that makes UI feel slow to open

definition: How long an animation takes
mechanics: total time of one animation leg
anti_patterns: fixed duration when distance varies wildly

definition: Whether an element holds the first or last keyframe before start / after end
expressions: flashes its final state before moving
mechanics: first/last keyframe styles applied outside the active phase
when_to_use: delayed items in a stagger or sequence
anti_patterns: forgetting forwards on draw sequences

definition: Animation divided into discrete jumps like a countdown
anti_patterns: stepping what should flow

definition: The one element the user must notice - the main actor of a group
mechanics: moves first · travels farthest · stays longest
anti_patterns: two elements competing for lead (a hierarchy problem motion cannot fix)

definition: Secondary content that follows the lead
mechanics: shorter and smaller motion after lead
anti_patterns: support moving as much as the lead (noise)

definition: Pills · badges · accents · dividers that only fade or do nothing
anti_patterns: decorations travelling distance (competition with lead)

definition: Everything deliberately not animated · including containers whose content animates
when_to_use: most groups shrink here at cast time
anti_patterns: animating a container and its children as two entrance layers

definition: Two elements share start and one timing family because they are one object or one moment
mechanics: same duration · same easing family · techniques may differ
when_to_use: paired parts (drawer height + its content · chip leaving + gap closing)
anti_patterns: mismatched clocks inside one object (the usual "something feels off")

definition: The second starts while the first is still moving — a stagger
mechanics: order without meaning is just delay · so overlap instead of sequence
anti_patterns: uniform gaps (metronome) · long waits for late items (cap the tail)

definition: The second starts as (or just before) the first finishes because order carries meaning
expressions: one after the other · handoff · domino
mechanics: handoff should overlap slightly to read as one gesture
when_to_use: draws · cause→effect · two rich views in one resizing box
anti_patterns: sequencing when order carries no meaning (that is a queue)

definition: Animate the parent and let children ride along when a child's path cannot be controlled directly
when_to_use: items flying into a bin · shared-layout landings
anti_patterns: tuning every child individually when the parent move does it in one

definition: Several animations share start and end timing even if their techniques differ
anti_patterns: different clocks inside one group

definition: Animations follow one another in order with handoff
mechanics: order carries meaning · causal or hierarchical chains
anti_patterns: chains over five items without grouping

definition: Acting on one element causes corresponding effects on related elements
anti_patterns: unbounded reach · never resetting after fast pointer exit

definition: A container's entrance and a stagger of its children never both animate
mechanics: the parent slides · the items are already there
anti_patterns: sliding panel + trickling items = two entrance layers the user waits through

definition: A good sequence reads as one gesture (wave)
expressions: a bad one as people waiting (queue)
synonyms: it reads as one thing; feels like a line
when_to_use: the judgement criterion for any timeline
anti_patterns: full handoff gaps (queue) · same-speed-everything (metronome)

definition: One group or component shares one duration + one easing curve family
expressions: same clock · feels like one object
mechanics: inner animations may use a lighter curve of the same family
anti_patterns: ease-in-out body inside ease-out container (out of sync feel)

definition: Exiting element leaves the layout flow immediately so siblings close the gap while it fades
mechanics: position taken out at removal moment
anti_patterns: sync mode stacking old + new (slow-feeling swap)

definition: One view fades out as another fades in at the same spot
mechanics: old exits while new enters (not one after the other)
anti_patterns: waiting for exit before entering (that is sequence)

definition: Delays that shrink across the group or vary by importance
mechanics: stagger with ease or manual importance steps
anti_patterns: equal gaps at every index (metronome)

definition: An idle animation inviting interaction waits before its first run and repeats rarely
expressions: occasionally taps · wiggles on its own
related: idle animation · repeat delay · first delay
mechanics: ~2.5s before first run · ~6s between runs · stops during interaction
when_to_use: hands · hint icons on fresh screens
anti_patterns: loops that fight user input or never pause

definition: Move an element along X or Y
when_to_use: everything that should not touch layout
anti_patterns: animating top/left instead (layout thrash)

definition: Make an element bigger or smaller
anti_patterns: scaling text-heavy blocks (re-flow blur)

definition: Spin an element around a point
anti_patterns: spinning content the user must read

definition: Slant an element shearing it out of rectangular shape
anti_patterns: skew on text (distorts reading)

definition: Rotate in 3D (rotateX/Y) to add depth
anti_patterns: 3D on dense functional UI

definition: How strong the 3D effect looks
anti_patterns: inconsistent perspective across siblings

definition: The anchor point a scale or rotation grows or spins from
anti_patterns: growing from the element's own center instead of its trigger

definition: An element animates out of its trigger rather than its own center
expressions: grows from where it was summoned from
anti_patterns: menu growing from viewport center

definition: A change that keeps the user oriented by visually connecting before and after
expressions: it follows where it came from
mechanics: before and after share position · identity or path
when_to_use: any state change of a persistent object
anti_patterns: teleporting between positions

definition: One shape smoothly turns into another
anti_patterns: morphing incompatible complex paths for spectacle

definition: A trigger grows in place into the surface it summons
anti_patterns: the trigger duplicating into a new copy

definition: An element travels and transforms from one position into another
mechanics: same identity rendered at both places
anti_patterns: duplicating the element as two unconnected animations

definition: An element animates to its new size/position instead of snapping
mechanics: measure old → apply new → invert → play
anti_patterns: animating every layout pass (unintended motion)

definition: First-Last-Invert-Play: measure before/after · animate the delta on transform only
mechanics: transform animation standing in for a layout move
anti_patterns: re-tweening layout properties per frame

definition: A section expands and collapses to show or hide content
anti_patterns: hard-cutting content into existence

definition: Content slides one way going forward and the opposite going back
expressions: next goes left · back comes from the left
mechanics: direction value read by enter AND exit
anti_patterns: forward and back sliding the same way

definition: A direction/state value passed to presence so exits read the latest context
anti_patterns: exit animating with the stale direction from mount

definition: Render the active view twice (one enters · the absolute twin only exits) to crossfade where naive stacking breaks
expressions: keep the fade in a morphing box
mechanics: exiting copy scales toward the next size
when_to_use: crossfading between two rich states in a resizing container
anti_patterns: scaling the visible copy during its enter

definition: Elements fade or slide into place as they enter the viewport
anti_patterns: replaying on scroll up (once only)

definition: Animation progress tied directly to scroll position
mechanics: scroll offset maps to timeline position
anti_patterns: driving layout properties from scroll

definition: Background and foreground move at different speeds while scrolling
anti_patterns: parallax on functional UI or over strong motion-sickness risk

definition: An animation playing when navigating between pages or routes
mechanics: exit old route + enter new (or none)
anti_patterns: transitioning every navigation at full length

definition: The browser morphs between two states or pages connecting shared elements
anti_patterns: depending on it without a fallback

definition: Visual change when the cursor moves over an element
anti_patterns: hover-only affordances on touch devices

definition: Subtle scale-down on click so the element feels physical
anti_patterns: pressing entire large containers

definition: A progress effect fills while the user holds a button
anti_patterns: infinite hold requirements

definition: Moving an element by grabbing it · often with momentum on release
anti_patterns: easing a dragged element away from the pointer

definition: Dragging list items rearranges them while others shift to make room
anti_patterns: siblings jumping without transition

definition: Dragging an element off-screen to close it
anti_patterns: dismiss with no velocity/position decision logic

definition: Resistance and snap-back when dragging past a boundary
anti_patterns: hard stops (feels broken) · infinite overrun

definition: A discrete stop a control settles onto when released
anti_patterns: detents that fight mid-range adjustment

definition: Blurring and fading everything around the focused item instead of dimming the whole page
anti_patterns: dimming the full viewport for one element

definition: Quick side-to-side jitter signaling an error or rejected input
anti_patterns: shake as ambient motion

definition: A circle expanding from the tap point confirming the press
anti_patterns: ripple on every hover-capable click

definition: The rate at which an animation speeds up or slows down
anti_patterns: linear on UI (reads mechanical)

definition: Starts fast · ends slow
when_to_use: almost everything on UI — the response begins instantly
anti_patterns: ease-in on entrances (delays the watched moment)

definition: Starts slow · ends fast
anti_patterns: ease-in on UI entrances

definition: Slow · fast · slow
anti_patterns: both-end dwell on frequent changes

definition: Constant speed
anti_patterns: linear for entrances (metronome feel)

definition: A curve defined by control points for precise control
anti_patterns: arbitrary curves nobody can feel

definition: A curve that accelerates and decelerates at different rates
when_to_use: entrances that must feel instant but land soft
anti_patterns: symmetric curves on response moments

definition: Motion driven by physics (tension · mass · damping) instead of a fixed duration
anti_patterns: springs on properties that need exact end-times

definition: How strongly the spring pulls toward target
anti_patterns: stiffness tuned per component ad hoc

definition: How quickly a spring settles
anti_patterns: zero damping on functional UI

definition: How heavy the animated element feels
when_to_use: differentiating big surfaces vs small controls
anti_patterns: mass as a per-widget toy

definition: Overshoot-and-settle adding playfulness
anti_patterns: the same bounce on everything (size-dependent reading)

definition: How long a spring feels finished though it keeps micro-settling
mechanics: tuned by observing where attention stops
anti_patterns: reading the raw simulation end as the perceived end

definition: Motion carrying velocity · especially after a drag or interruption
anti_patterns: stopping dead at release

definition: How fast and which direction an element is moving
anti_patterns: position animations that restart from zero velocity

definition: An animation that can be smoothly redirected mid-flight
anti_patterns: queues that must finish before the next input

definition: Re-triggering a sequence mid-flight must stop in-flight motion and replay cleanly · never stack
expressions: what if I click twice fast
mechanics: kill running animations before new ones
anti_patterns: testing only the happy path (the bug lives in the second click)

definition: Content scrolling continuously in a loop
anti_patterns: marquee on functional content

definition: An animation repeating a number of times or forever
anti_patterns: loops without pause-on-interaction duty

definition: A loop that plays forward then reverses each iteration
anti_patterns: alternating loops whose halves use different clocks

definition: An element circling around another continuously
anti_patterns: orbit as primary loading signal

definition: A gentle repeating scale or opacity change to draw attention
anti_patterns: pulses that compete for lead with content

definition: Gentle continuous up-down drift making a static element feel alive
anti_patterns: floating functional controls

definition: Subtle motion while an element waits to be interacted with
anti_patterns: loops that never pause

definition: A filter softening an element or hiding imperfections
anti_patterns: blurring large surfaces per frame (expensive)

definition: Clipping an element to a shape
anti_patterns: clip on every element (paint cost)

definition: Hiding or revealing parts with a shape or gradient with soft edges
anti_patterns: using mask when a clip reads better

definition: A draggable divider wiping between two overlaid images
anti_patterns: non-draggable comparison UI

definition: An SVG path draws itself as if a pen traced it
anti_patterns: drawing full pages of paths

definition: Setting pathLength=100 so stroke math uses round numbers regardless of real length
mechanics: engine maps declared length to real geometry
anti_patterns: hardcoding per-path dasharray numbers

definition: Text animating character by character when it changes
anti_patterns: long paragraphs (unreadable mid-state)

definition: A placeholder with a moving sheen while content loads
anti_patterns: shimmer competing as decoration

definition: Digits rolling or counting up to a value
anti_patterns: tickers implying progress they do not have

definition: Digits rolling vertically in the direction the value moved
anti_patterns: rolling full strings per keystroke

definition: Fixed-width digits so changing numbers do not shift layout
anti_patterns: proportional digits reflowing mid-animation

definition: Text appearing one character at a time
anti_patterns: typewriting paragraphs users must read

definition: Motion passing its target before settling
anti_patterns: overshoot on precise positioning

definition: The brief suspension at the apex of an arc before descent
anti_patterns: uniform speed through the apex

definition: Real objects move along curves not straight lines
mechanics: compose X and Y with different curves
anti_patterns: dead-straight translations in physical contexts

definition: A smaller accompanying motion that gives the main one life
mechanics: small delayed or offset sibling animation
when_to_use: icons with trailing lines · hair on a head-turn
anti_patterns: secondary action competing with the lead

definition: A small wind-up opposite a move
mechanics: brief reverse motion before the main one
anti_patterns: anticipation on frequent UI

definition: Parts keep moving and settle slightly after the main motion stops
anti_patterns: rigid whole-block stops everywhere

definition: Deforming an element in flight to convey weight and speed
anti_patterns: deforming text or readable content

definition: Frames drawn per second
anti_patterns: accepting jank as a feel detail

definition: Visible stutter when the browser drops frames
anti_patterns: chasing FPS instead of the dropped frames

definition: A frame the browser missed its deadline to draw
anti_patterns: assuming every drop is visible

definition: The GPU moves/fades an element on its own layer without relayout
when_to_use: all motion that should be smooth
anti_patterns: layer explosion (memory)

definition: A CSS hint that an element is about to animate
mechanics: promotes the element to its own GPU layer ahead of the animation
when_to_use: just-in-time promotion before an animation starts
anti_patterns: never as a permanent style

definition: Animating layout properties forcing recalculation every frame
mechanics: layout+paint run inside the frame loop
anti_patterns: animating height on containers as a rule (see layout_exception)

definition: Motion serves a function not decoration
mechanics: animation answers an orientation or feedback need
anti_patterns: decoration-only motion

definition: The right animation makes an interface feel faster than it is
anti_patterns: animation as cover for real slowness

definition: The more often an animation is seen the shorter and subtler it should be
mechanics: exposure count sets the budget tier
anti_patterns: full entrances on menus and palettes

definition: An element keeps identity and position across states so users never lose track
mechanics: the object's path or anchor survives the change
anti_patterns: teleporting the same object

definition: Animating transform and opacity lets the GPU keep motion smooth
anti_patterns: animating filter/clip at scale without measuring

definition: Respecting the user's reduced-motion setting
mechanics: drop delays and movement · keep opacity
anti_patterns: merely shortening durations as the concession

definition: Under reduce · choreography collapses (no stagger · no sequence) instead of only shortening
anti_patterns: frame-by-frame sequences surviving reduce (jump their frames instead)

definition: Stepping through a recording frame by frame to judge motion
mechanics: capture at high fps · inspect moments
when_to_use: any choreography claim ("it reads as a wave")
anti_patterns: judging motion at full speed from memory

definition: One row per moving element: role · start · duration · motion · relationship
mechanics: written before implementation · checked against budgets
anti_patterns: coding timings then documenting them after

definition: Secondary motion lands on the event it belongs to · not the previous trigger
expressions: the pulse is on the click
anti_patterns: hover-then-click backgrounds pulsing on hover

definition: Sparkles and motion lines complete as the lead finishes (last ~20% of its timeline)
mechanics: accent keyframes squeezed into the lead's final window
when_to_use: emphasis effects on arrivals and impacts
anti_patterns: accents timed by feel that drift from the lead

definition: Once a hover state is set a follow-up click plays immediately with same proportions earlier
mechanics: shift the whole thing earlier · keep internal ratios
anti_patterns: rebuilding the entrance on every repeat

definition: Duration derives from the delta of the change not a fixed number
anti_patterns: one fixed fade for every jump size

definition: Smaller elements need more bounce to read alive
anti_patterns: one bounce value making big views feel heavy or slow

definition: With a small finite state set · hand-tuned values beat a clever formula
expressions: a dozen tuned beats one formula
anti_patterns: formulas nobody can fine-tune to feel right

definition: Short punchy streaks around an action conveying force
mechanics: burst completing at the lead's landing
anti_patterns: lines that outlive the moment they punctuate

definition: A thing that slid in from the right leaves toward the right
expressions: back out the way it came
anti_patterns: fade-only exits for slid-in objects (the object teleports)

definition: Groups leaving do so at once · shorter and simpler than their entrance
mechanics: single shared exit clock without handoffs
anti_patterns: reverse-staggering things out
